raw_response:
I plant cotton every year, same as always. My man and me, we farm 10.9 mu together. I been doing this 46 years, I know my land.

I start like I always start. I buy the cotton seed from the dealer in town — the good kind with the worm protection, the Bt one. Everyone around here plants that. The old cotton without it, the bollworm eats you alive, you spray and spray and still lose half. So I pay more for the good seed, it saves trouble.

For fertilizer, I do what I always do. Before planting, I spread 2 bags of compound fertilizer each mu — the 15-15-15 kind, that's 100 jin per bag so about 50 kg. Then when the cotton is growing and setting bolls, in July when it's hot, I put urea down the row, maybe half a bag each mu, so 20-25 kg. If the plants look yellow I add a little more. My neighbor's wife, she puts less and her cotton doesn't make good bolls. I rather spend the money on fertilizer than see small bolls. Losing yield is worse than spending a few hundred yuan extra.

I plough the land in spring before planting — my son-in-law brings the tractor, we pay him for the fuel. Then we plant in rows, cover with plastic film, that's what keeps the ground warm and wet.

Water — I got the well, so I water when it's dry. Usually 3 times, maybe 4 if the sky don't rain. Once before flowering, once during flowering, once when bolls are filling. Water costs electricity, I don't waste it.

Pesticide — cotton has many pests. Aphids first when plants are small, then bollworm even with Bt seed, then spider mites in hot weather. I spray maybe 6, 7 times over the season. I mix what the shop man gives me. Some years more if pests come bad.

Two of us can't pick 10.9 mu alone at harvest. I call my daughter and some women from the village, pay them by the jin picked. That's the biggest labor cost.

Good year I get maybe 250 kg seed cotton each mu. Bad year, 200. I aim for around 260.
